J1.evidence: Belagat «فلا تزال تعب في الشراب»: unvowelled تعب is simply تَعُبّ (from عبّ, to gulp) written without shadda, so TR 'durmadan kana kana içerler' translates what is written; no silent correction occurred. The other point (auditory masdar) concerns EN only. Rest of TR checked (i'rab, sarf, fawaid) and matches the Arabic.

J2.evidence: Arabic «فلا تزال تعب في الشراب» is unvocalized تَعُبّ (to gulp) written without shadda, not a defect; TR 'suyu durmadan kana kana içerler' translates what is written, no correction and no note needed. TR Sarf '(55) شرب: ... semâî masdarıdır' correctly renders مصدر سماعي.

J1.evidence: Morphology «(55) شرب: مصدر سماعي للثلاثي شرب» is rendered 'an auditory maṣdar'; سماعي here means non-analogical/transmitted (as opposed to قياسي), and 'auditory' (relating to hearing) gives a wrong meaning. Should be e.g. 'a non-analogical (samāʿī) maṣdar'. (The EN note on تعب is marked and harmless.)

J2.evidence: EN Morphology renders «مصدر سماعي» as 'an auditory maṣdar'; سماعي here means non-analogical (transmitted/heard from the Arabs, vs قياسي), 'auditory' misleads. Also the EN Translator's note falsely claims the source reads تعب 'to be wearied': «تعب في الشراب» is simply unpointed تعبّ (gulp), so the note misstates the source and should be removed.
